topic.name: Determining Indexes of Terms in Arithmetic Sequences

question.text: What is the index of the term $\dfrac{79}{2}$ for the arithmetic sequence below? \[ a_{n+1} = a_n + 1, \quad a_1 = \dfrac{1}{2},\quad n\geq 1 \]
question.explanation:
We will convert the recursive formula to an explicit formula and then solve for the value of $n$ such that $a_n=\dfrac{79}2.$

The recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence takes the form \[ a_{n+1} = a_n +d. \]

In the given formula, we have $d=1.$ We are also told that $a_1=\dfrac 1 2,$ so we can write the explicit formula as follows:

\begin{align*} a_n &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= \dfrac 1 2 + (n-1)(1) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 1 2+ n - 1 \\[5pt] &= n - \dfrac 12 \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ such that $a_n=\dfrac{79}2\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} a_n &= n - \dfrac 12 \\[5pt] \dfrac {79}2 &= n - \dfrac 12 \\[5pt] \dfrac {79}2 + \dfrac 12 &= n \\[3pt] 40 &= n \end{align*}

Therefore, $\dfrac{79}2$ is the $40$th term of the sequence.

example.title: Determining the Index of a Term Given the Recursive Formula

question.text:
What is the index of the term $-62$ for the arithmetic sequence below?

\[ f(n+1) = f(n) - 4, \quad f(1) = 30,\quad n\geq 1 \]
question.explanation:
We will convert the recursive formula to an explicit formula and then solve for the value of $n$ such that $f(n)=-62.$

The recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence takes the form \[ f(n+1) = f(n) +d. \]

In the given formula, we have $d=-4.$ We are also told that $f(1)=30,$ so we can write the explicit formula as follows:

\begin{align*} f(n) &= f(1) + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= 30 + (n-1)(-4) \\[3pt] &= 30 - 4n + 4 \\[3pt] &= 34 - 4n \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ such that $f(n)=-62 \mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f(n) &= 34-4n \\[3pt] -62 &= 34-4n \\[3pt] -96 &= -4n \\[3pt] \dfrac{-96}{-4} &= n \\[3pt] 24 &= n \end{align*}

Therefore, $-62$ is the $24$th term of the sequence.

example.title: Determining the Index of a Term Given the Recursive Formula

question.text: Given an arithmetic sequence that has $a_3=-5$ and common difference $d=2,$ what is the index of the term $99?$
question.explanation:
Since $a_3=-5$ is $2$ jumps after $a_1,$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

\begin{align*} a_3 &= a_1 + 2d \\[3pt] -5 &= a_1 + 2(2) \\[3pt] -5 &= a_1 + 4 \\[3pt] -9 &= a_1 \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

\begin{align*} a_{n} &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= -9 + (n-1)(2) \\[3pt] &= -9 + 2n - 2 \\[3pt] &= 2n - 11 \end{align*}

Now, we solve for the value of $n$ that gives $a_n=99,$ as follows:

\begin{align*} a_{n} &= 2n - 11 \\[3pt] 99 &= 2n - 11 \\[3pt] 110 &= 2n \\[3pt] \dfrac{110}{2} &= n \\[3pt] 55 &= n \end{align*}

Therefore, $99$ is the $55$th term of the sequence.
